n: The famine continued without relief, forcing the family to face the hard decision they had put off.
Once the grain ran out, Jacob asked his sons to go back to Egypt—as if Benjamin’s condition could be ignored.
Judah takes the lead now, reminding his father that the Egyptian lord had sworn they would not be received without Benjamin.
Judah says plainly: if Benjamin comes, we will go and buy food.
Without Benjamin, there is no point in going. Judah respectfully but firmly forces the decision.
Jacob—called Israel here, as he begins to act in faith—complains that they should never have mentioned another brother.

f.w: Wherefore dealt ye so ill with me
f.g: Why did you treat me so badly

n: The brothers explain the man questioned them closely about their family; they could not have known what he would demand.
Judah pleads for the whole family’s survival—their children included. Keeping Benjamin home would mean everyone starving.

f.w: that we may live, and not die

n: Judah pledges himself as security for Benjamin and accepts lifelong blame if he fails. This Judah, who once sold a brother, now offers himself for one.

f.g: a guarantee; one who takes personal responsibility for another

n: Judah notes they could have gone and returned twice by now if they hadn’t delayed.
Jacob relents and, as he once did with Esau, sends a gift: the best products of Canaan—balm, honey, spices, nuts.
Jacob tells them to take double money and return what was found in their sacks—honesty even when it might be an error.
Finally Jacob releases Benjamin into their care.
Jacob prays that “God Almighty” (El Shaddai, the covenant name used in his blessings) will grant mercy. Then he submits: if I lose my children, I lose them.

f.w: If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved

n: The brothers set out with the gift, double money, and Benjamin, and stood before Joseph again.
When Joseph saw Benjamin, he ordered his steward to prepare a feast at his house for the men at noon.

f.g: slaughter an animal and prepare a meal

n: The steward obeyed and brought the brothers into Joseph’s home.
Instead of feeling honored, they feared a trap: maybe they would be seized as slaves over the returned money. Guilt makes people expect punishment.

f.g: look for a pretext to accuse us

n: Before going in, they nervously approached the steward at the doorway to explain themselves.
They begin explaining their first trip politely and carefully.
They tell how they found all their money in their sacks and have brought it back in full.

f.g: Money was silver weighed out, not coins.

n: They insist they have new money for this purchase and don’t know who put the old money back.
The steward calms them with “Peace be to you” and credits their God with the gift. Joseph may have taught him about the God of Israel. Then Simeon is released.
They were treated as honored guests: water to wash their feet and feed for their animals.
They arranged their gift and waited for Joseph to arrive at noon.
When Joseph came, they bowed to the ground before him—the dream fulfilled once more, now with all eleven present.

f.w: bowed themselves to him to the earth

n: Joseph asks warmly about their father, the old man—barely hiding his own deep concern.
They reply that their father is well and bow again.
Joseph sees Benjamin, his only full brother, for the first time in over twenty years and blesses him tenderly.

f.g: his full brother; both were sons of Rachel

n: Overcome with emotion, Joseph hurried to a private room to weep.

f.g: his deepest feelings were stirred; Hebrew uses the inner organs for emotion

n: He washed his face, regained control, and ordered the meal served.
Seating followed Egyptian custom: Joseph ate apart as a high official, the Egyptians apart from the Hebrews, whom they considered ritually unclean to eat with.
The brothers were seated in exact birth order, oldest to youngest. They stared at each other in amazement—how could this stranger know?
Joseph sent portions from his table, giving Benjamin five times as much—perhaps a test of whether the brothers would resent a favored son again. This time they simply feasted.
